source: Season 28 supplementary ordinary Java panel C is development data. Use all 48 paired native client and server calendars, 24 per RTT. The calendar bank contains only poll timestamps, relative to the first client poll, through 61 samples per stream. Later simulated ticks repeat the last 20 intervals. No actions, health, bout lengths or outcome labels enter the bank.
validation: Use the next scout and the next two available ordinary promotion panels after season 28. Their native calendars are reserved. With the first registration for each panel, generate predictions from its publicly declared openings before inspecting its native results. Restrict comparisons to the same qualified native cells as the promotion. No evaluation calendar can enter the frozen bank.
hypothesis: Paired empirical variability of the two clients and server transfers to new ordinary Java bouts better than separately jittering one client poll per nominal tick.
score: Compare mean squared error against the 1, 0.5, 0 Java points within each prospective panel. Score each qualified player arm once, including W-tap, and show matched expected points and W-tap by RTT. The reference is the existing queued phase clock, with fixed timing also reported. Both variable models share the existing packet queue, timing jitter for transit, game rules, distribution of hidden entity-update order and 128 trials per bout.
scope: This is a prediction experiment. No change to play, training, or promotion is made from these calendars. A missing second independent promotion panel is reported if the league ends first. This small bank comes from one headless host session and cannot establish broad deployment parity.
